To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the vagal modulation of the heart rate is decreased after vasovagal episodes in young patients but not in elderly patients, and that the time-domain analysis of heart rate variability is a useful tool to detect the recent occurrence of vasovagal synope in young patients.
the parasympathetically mediated modulation of the heart rate decreases after a vasovagal synope, and that this reduction is age-related.
the time-domain analysis of heart rate variability is useful to identify patients with recent vasvagal syncope, and that this analysis is not age-independent.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new methods for the analysis of the heart rate variability in order to differentiate between healthy subjects and patients with recent vasodilatative syncope, and to investigate the influence of age on the cardiac parasympatic modulation.
the analysis of the heart rate variability and the heart rate turbulence in patients with vasovagal synocope and healthy subjects.
the study of the autonomic nervous system, in particular the vagal modulation of cardiac function, by using the time and frequency domain analysis of 24-hours ECG recordings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the parasympathetically modulated cardiac function is impaired after a syncopal event, but that this impairment is only significant in young patients.
the time-domain analysis of HRV is not suitable to differentiate healthy subjects from those with recent vasovasal syncope in the elderly population.

patients with recent vasodepressor syncope can be identified by a reduction of vagal modulation of the heart rate in the time domain analysis of 24 hours electrocardiographic recording up to an age of 40, whereas this is no longer possible in the elderly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the time domain analysis is not a suitable method for detecting vasovagal syncope in elderly patients.

patients with recent vasvagal syncope can not be differentiated from healthy controls with time-domain analysis of heart rate variability, because the age-related changes of vagal modulation of the heart rate are similar in both groups.
vasovagal syncope is associated with a transient reduction of cardiac vagal activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the time-domain analysis of the heart rate variability is not a reliable marker for vasovagal syncope.
we can use a non-invasive method to detect a change in the autonomic nervous system after vasovagal syncopal attacks.
age-related changes of cardiac vagal modulation are important to consider when studying the pathogenesis of vasovagal syncope.
